Top candidates: Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot, Southern_Blight, Southern_Bacterial_Wilt.

Let me check reference images one at a time.

This reference (1568067) is extremely close to the test image (1568068) — consecutive Bugwood IDs, same photographer/study, same visual context (stem pulled from ground with roots, white material at soil line). Strong Southern_Blight signal. Let me continue with more classes.

**Analysis summary:**

The test image (Bugwood 1568068) shows a tomato plant pulled from sandy soil with the stem split longitudinally at the soil line. Key features: white/chalky material on the lower stem exterior, brown collapsed root system, dead leaves, classic stem-base disease.

**Strongest match:** Southern_Blight reference Bugwood_48 (ID 1568067) — a consecutive Bugwood ID from the same photographer/study. It shows an identical scene: stem pulled from sandy soil with roots attached and white material at the stem base. All other classes were clearly different (microscopy images, leaf spots, vascular discoloration in clean lab settings, etc.).

The white material at the soil-line stem in the test image is consistent with *Sclerotium rolfsii* mycelium, and the plant completely collapsed at the base. No sclerotia were visible in this frame but the overall presentation (stem girdling at soil line, white fungal coating, sandy soil, dead plant) perfectly matches Southern_Blight.
